pr_title: Clear ActiveRecord object memoized by take
pr_body:
### Summary
`ActiveRecord` object is memoized when `take` is called on a relation which is returned when `where/find_by` is called on the same relation.
This memoized state of the object needs to be cleared.

Fixes #36977

issue_context.title: Memoization issue with `take` resulting in returning wrongly memoized ActiveRecord object on query using find_by/where
issue_context.body:
### Script to reproduce
<!-- (Guidelines for creating a bug report are [available
here](https://edgeguides.rubyonrails.org/contributing_to_ruby_on_rails.html#creating-a-bug-report)) -->
```ruby
# frozen_string_literal: true

require "bundler/inline"

gemfile(true) do
  source "https://rubygems.org"
  ruby "2.6.3"

  gem "sqlite3"
  gem "rails", '6.0.0'
end

require "active_record"
require "minitest/autorun"

# This connection will do for database-independent bug reports.
ActiveRecord::Base.establish_connection(adapter: "sqlite3", database: "bug_test")
ActiveRecord::Base.logger = Logger.new(STDOUT)

ActiveRecord::Schema.define do
  create_table :posts, force: true do |t|
    t.string :name
  end
end

class Post < ActiveRecord::Base
end

class BugTest < Minitest::Test
  def setup
    10.times do |idx|
      Post.create!(name: idx.to_s)
    end
    @posts = Post.all
    # Pick any arbitrary post using take
    @cached_post = @posts.take
  end

  def test_issue_with_where
    10.times do |idx|
      post_name = idx.to_s
      # Skip for cached post name
      next if post_name == @cached_post.name

      # Get the specific post with name `idx`
      # The post returned will be the cached one since rails is caching the
      # output of take on https://github.com/rails/rails/blob/b9ca94caea2ca6a6cc09abaffaad67b447134079/activerecord/lib/active_record/relation/finder_methods.rb#L504
      idx_post = @posts.where(name: post_name).take

      # This assertion should fail whereas it's passing right now because of
      # memoization by take
      assert_equal post_name, idx_post.name

      # Since memoized post is being returned by take, object_id will be same
      assert @cached_post.object_id != idx_post.object_id
    end
  end

  def test_issue_with_find_by
    10.times do |idx|
      post_name = idx.to_s
      # Skip for cached post name
      next if post_name == @cached_post.name

      idx_post = @posts.find_by(name: post_name)

      # This assertion should fail whereas it's passing right now because of
      # memoization by take
      assert_equal post_name, idx_post.name

      # Since memoized post is being returned by take, object_id will be same
      assert @cached_post.object_id != idx_post.object_id
    end
  end
end
```
All the assertions in the above script should be false whereas they are true because of the bug


Problem is with this line
https://github.com/rails/rails/blob/b9ca94caea2ca6a6cc09abaffaad67b447134079/activerecord/lib/active_record/relation/finder_methods.rb#L504

### Expected behavior
<!-- Tell us what should happen -->
Every time `find_by` or `where` is called on an ActiveRecord relation, it should query the DB every time

### Actual behavior
<!-- Tell us what happens instead -->
Querying ActiveRecord relation returns the ActiveRecord object memoized by `take` if `take` was called on the relation before query using `find_by` or `where`

### System configuration
**Rails version**:
6.0.0

**Ruby version**:
2.6.3
comments: @anmolarora are these assertions supposed to fail on 6.0? They're passing for me.
The assertions are supposed to fail instead they are passing. That's the problem. @eileencodes
Ok. This passes on all versions of Rails I tested, 5.2, 6.0, and master. Is this a change in behavior or just a bug you noticed?
This is a bug. As I've mentioned that `take` is memoizing the ActiveRecord object and after calling `take` every `where/find_by` query is returning the memoized object on the relation
Is there a version of Rails this script should fail in?
I've updated the script to make it fail. This should make the bug clearly visible.

It looks like this has been broken forever / since 1379375f93c53d4c49fa8592b6117c3ade263f2e :confused:

`@take` should be cleared in `ActiveRecord::Relation#reset`: https://github.com/rails/rails/blob/6b40767df8635125c62b550d2652074d2e6daf03/activerecord/lib/active_record/relation.rb#L638-L645

review_comments: Let's put an `order(:title)` on here, otherwise the test will fail sporadically when the database happens to return "3" in the first `take`

There is only one Post in the DB with title '3'. 
Will this still be a problem?

Oh, sorry, I was concerned that "3" might get [legitimately] chosen as `first_post`, and then the `assert_not_equal` would fail -- but it's comparing `object_id`, so it will actually be fine even if they both contain the same row. :+1:
